summary: Iteration 6: membership downgrade guard + /plans UX follow-ups VERIFIED. BACKEND 38/38 PASSED (test_membership_upgrade.py 11/11 incl. new downgrade-block tests, test_jobradar.py 27/27). Active Annual -> checkout Quarterly/Half = 400 'You can switch to a shorter plan after your current plan expires...'; payments stay at 1; subscription count, plan_id, expiry and subscription_id unchanged; Annual sub stays 'active'. Half->Quarterly = 400, then Half->Annual = today+365. Quarterly->Annual = today+365, then Annual renewal = today+730. Downgrade after expire_now is allowed (today+90). Unknown plan = 404. Dev panel activate/renew still work and bypass the guard (activate_365 -> simulate_renewal 730 -> activate_90 replaces to today+90 -> reset). Returning to /plans preselects Annual with renewal note; Half and Quarterly both show the switch-later note with the button disabled. Note text is #1F2937 on #FEF3C7, good contrast. No deprecated Expo packages in the reviewed file.

issues: ScrollView paddingBottom is insets.bottom+120, but the bottom bar is about 115px with a 2-line note (policy text ends at y=724, bar starts at about 729 on 390x844). A 3-line note (numberOfLines=3, long plan names or narrow screens) would cover the end of the policy text. Consider about 160px of padding, or measure the bar with onLayout.
Bottom-bar note has no background or icon, so it reads as plain text. Optional: reuse the amber banner style for consistency with the top note.

action_items: Minor: increase /plans ScrollView paddingBottom (or use the bottom bar's onLayout height) so a 3-line plan-change-note-bottom never covers the last content
Optional: when checkout-btn is disabled for a shorter plan, consider a 'Renew current plan' shortcut or changing the button label (e.g. 'Available after current plan expires')
critical_code_review_comments: server.py checkout_demo: guard runs before the payment insert, so blocked downgrades create no payment or email. Correct.

The guard compares duration_days of the current and target plans. If an admin later makes two plans with equal duration, a switch between them is treated as an upgrade (today+duration, remaining days lost). Acceptable edge case.
server.py is 1500+ lines (above the 700-line guideline). Consider splitting the membership/checkout/admin-dev routes into modules.
plans.tsx: the effect on [mem.is_active, mem.plan_id] resets the selection only when the membership's plan changes, not on every refetch. Fine.
